'''Zachry Cheyne Edey''' ({{IPAc-en|'|iː|d|i}} {{respell|EE|dee}}; born May 14, 2002) is a Canadian [[college basketball]] player for the [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. He is listed at {{convert|7|ft|4|in|m}}, making him the tallest player in Big Ten history. At the close of the 2023 season, Edey was named the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]] and [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|consensus National Player of the Year]]. He repeated as Big Ten Player of the Year and consensus National Player of the Year in 2024.

Edey also represents [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canada]] in international competition.

==Early life and high school career==
Zachry Cheyne Edey was born in [[Toronto]] on May 14, 2002, to Julia and Glen Edey.<ref name="bio"/><ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.imgacademy.com/sites/default/files/img-2020-commencement-program.pdf|title=Twentieth Annual Commencement Ceremony|date=June 5, 2020|publisher=IMG Academy|accessdate=March 31, 2024}}</ref> His {{convert|6|ft|3|in|adj=on}} mother was born to Chinese immigrants in Toronto, where she grew up and played basketball;<ref name=norlander_02282023>{{Cite web |first=Matt|last=Norlander|title=Simple, but not easy: After rejecting basketball for years, Zach Edey's Zen-like approach made him unstoppable |date=February 8, 2023| url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/simple-but-not-easy-after-rejecting-basketball-for-years-zach-edeys-zen-like-approach-made-him-unstoppable/ |access-date=March 12, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Abdulhamid|last=Ibrahim|title=With mom by his side, Canada's Zach Edey dominating college basketball|date=March 15, 2023|publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|agency=The Canadian Press|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/ncaa-basketball-zach-edey-mom-connection-1.6735847|access-date=March 15, |url=https://www.wishtv.com/sports/zach-edeys-unlikely-path-to-college-basketballs-most-interesting-player/ |access-date=March 16, 2023 |publisher=WISH-TV|language=en-US}}</ref> his father is white.<ref name=fader_03152023>{{cite web|first=Mirin|last=Fader|title=Zach Edey Is Just Different|date=March 15, 2023|work=The Ringer|url=https://www.theringer.com/2023/3/15/23640235/zach-edey-purdue-boilermakers|access-date=March 16, 2023}}</ref> Edey grew up playing [[ice hockey]] as well as [[baseball]], which his father Edey moved to the United States and attended [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]].<ref name=dopirak_11142019/> He joined their second-tier team in his first year, working daily with IMG coach and former [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player [[Daniel Santiago]]. Edey was promoted to the school's national team the following year.<ref name=fader_03152023/><ref name=dopirak_11142019>{{cite web |last=Dopirak |first=Dustin |title='It seems like a movie': Purdue's new big man Zach Edey was on skates until two years ago |url=https://theathletic.com/1366159/2019/11/14/it-seems-like-a-movie-purdues-new-big-man-zach-edey-was-on-skates-until-two-years-ago/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=June 10, 2021 |date=November 14, 2019}}</ref> A consensus three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2020 class and committed to playing college basketball for [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] over offers from [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] and [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]], among others.<ref>{{cite web |last=Carmin |first=Mike |title=Purdue basketball lands 7–6 Canadian big man Zach Edey |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2019/11/09/zach-edey-commits-purdue-basketball/2532883001/ |website=[[Journal & Courier]] |access-date=June 10, 2021 |date=November 9, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
===Freshman season===
In his [[freshman]] season at [[Purdue University]], Edey was listed at {{height|ft=7|in=4}}, making him the tallest player in [[Big Ten]] history.<ref>{{cite web |last=Doyel |first=Gregg |title=7–6!?! Purdue's Zach Edey is getting taller — and better. Where it ends, nobody knows. |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/columnists/gregg-doyel/2021/05/12/purdue-basketball-zach-edey-height-nba-draft-mlb-baseball-pitcher/5020015001/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=June 10, 2021 |date=May 12, 2021}}</ref> On March 2, 2021, he recorded a season-high 21 points and seven [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] off the bench in a 73–69 win over [[2020–21 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Polzin |first=Jim |title=Falling short: Badgers struggle to contain freshman center Zach Edey as Boilermakers hold on at home |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/college/basketball/men/falling-short-badgers-struggle-to-contain-freshman-center-zach-edey-as-boilermakers-hold-on-at/article_a3e314ab-1407-5213-b80e-4b9e8e5efa69.html |website=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |access-date=June 10, 2021 |date=March 3, 2021}}</ref> Sharing playing time with fellow center [[Trevion Williams]], he averaged 8.7 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.1 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] in 14 minutes per game, earning Big Ten All-Freshman Team honours.<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Zach Edey – Men's Basketball |url=https://purduesports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=11486|publisher=Purdue University Athletics |access-date=June 10, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Todd Aaron|last=Golden|title=Edey speaks softly, but carries weight with Purdue teammates|date=March 14, 2023|work=Tribune-Star|url=https://www.tribstar.com/indiana/sports/edey-speaks-softly-but-carries-weight-with-purdue-teammates/article_81f40fcf-b90d-5411-8fc7-dc39d7195992.html|access-date=March 15, 2023}}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
To begin his [[sophomore]] year, Edey moved into a starting role. On January 3, 2022, he recorded a then-career-high 24 points and 10 rebounds in 20 minutes in a 74–69 loss to [[2021–22 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Davis scores 37 in No. 23 Badgers' win over No. 3 Purdue |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364360 |access-date=March 12, 2022 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 3, 2022}}</ref> On February 26, 2022, Edey recorded a career-high 25 points in 22 minutes in a 68–65 loss to [[2021–22 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Michigan State snaps slump with 68–65 win over No. 4 Purdue |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364462 |access-date=March 12, 2022 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 26, 2022}}</ref> As a sophomore, he averaged career highs in every category except free throw percentage, averaging 14.4 points, 7.7 rebounds, 1.1 assists, and 1.2 blocks in only 19 minutes per game. Following the conclusion of the season, Edey was named to the Second Team All-Big Ten.<ref name=B10Awards>{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308180525/https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 8, 2022|title=2021–22 Big Ten Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}}</ref>

===Junior season===
On December 17, 2022, Edey became both the 55th player in Purdue's history to reach 1,000 career points<ref name="1000Points">{{cite magazine|last=Fezler|first=D.J.|title= Complete List of Purdue Men's Basketball All-Time 1,000-Point Scorers |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/complete-list-of-purdue-mens-basketball-all-time-1000-point-scorers |access-date=September 18, 2023 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 18, 2023}}</ref> and the 11th player in Purdue's history to reach 100 career blocks.<ref name="100Blocks">{{cite web |title=100 career rejections |url=https://twitter.com/BoilerBall/status/1604651482829279239|via=Twitter |access-date=December 18, 2022}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2024}}

During the [[2022–23 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|2022–23 season]], Edey received Big Ten Player of the Week six times,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Edey Picks Up 6th Big Ten Player of the Week Accolade |url=https://purduesports.com/news/2023/2/6/mens-basketball-edey-picks-up-6th-big-ten-player-of-the-week-accolade.aspx |access-date=February 27, 2023 |website=Purdue Boilermakers |language=en}}</ref> tying the school record for most awards in a single season ([[Caleb Swanigan]], 2016–17) and rising to second most all-time in men's basketball in the Big Ten ([[Evan Turner]], 2009–10).

At the close of the season, Edey was named the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]] and [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''Sporting News'' National Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news|last=DeCourcy|first=Mike|title= Purdue's Zach Edey is Sporting News' College Basketball Player of the Year |url= https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/purdues-zach-edey-sporting-news-college-basketball-player-year/nqnr5ziukkpzaadmy86v4aol |access-date=March 11, 2023 |work=[[Sporting News]]|date=March 8, 2023}}</ref> He was also named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].

===Senior season===
On May 31, 2023, Edey announced that he was opting out of the [[2023 NBA draft]] to return to Purdue for his [[senior (education)|senior]] season.<ref>{{cite news|last=Beard|first=Aaron|title= Purdue's Zach Edey opts to withdraw from NBA draft |url= https://www.nba.com/news/zach-edey-opts-to-return-to-purdue |access-date=September 18, 2023 |work=[[NBA]]|date=June 1, 2023}}</ref> On January 5, 2024, Edey became the second player in Purdue history to reach 1000 career rebounds, following [[Joe Barry Carroll]].<ref>{{cite news|last=King|first=Sam|title= No. 1 Purdue basketball passes latest test, topples Illinois in top-10 battle |url= https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2024/01/05/purdue-basketball-knocks-off-ninth-ranked-illinois/72115841007/ |access-date=January 9, 2024 |work=Journal & Courier|date=January 5, 2024}}</ref> On January 28, 2024, Edey scored 26 points in a win against [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball statistical leaders|Rutgers]] to surpass 2,000 for his collegiate career points, making him just the sixth player in Big Ten Conference history to have 2,000 points and 1,000 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 28, 2024 |title=Purdue's Edey joins 2K point-1K rebound club |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39411817/purdue-zach-edey-hits-2000-career-points-win-rutgers |access-date=January 31, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On February 4, in a win against Wisconsin, Edey set two different school records. He scored in double figures for the 74th consecutive game, passing [[Rick Mount]]. Edey also broke [[Terry Dischinger]]'s record for double-doubles as he secured the 55th of his career. In addition to his school records, he reached 200 career blocks in the game. That week, Edey was named Big Ten Player of the Week for the 10th time in his career. This tied [[Evan Turner]] for the most awards in Big Ten history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 5, 2024 |title=EDEY NABS LEAGUE-RECORD 10TH BIG TEN PLAYER OF THE WEEK HONOR |url=https://purduesports.com/news/2024/2/5/mens-basketball-edey-nabs-league-record-10th-big-ten-player-of-the-week-honor |access-date=February 6, 2024 |website=purduesports.com |language=en}}</ref>

Edey currently holds the record for rebounds at Purdue with 1,178, passing [[Joe Barry Carroll]] in a game against Ohio State on February 18, 2024.

On February 26, 2024, it was announced that Edey would not use his extra year of eligibility gained from COVID-19 to return to Purdue for the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boone |first=Kyle |date=February 26, 2024 |title=Zach Edey will not return to Purdue in 2024-25: Reigning national player of the year won't use extra season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/zach-edey-will-not-return-to-purdue-in-2024-25-reigning-national-player-of-the-year-wont-use-extra-season/ |access-date=February 27, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Edey represented [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|Canada]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in Latvia. He averaged 15.1 points, a tournament-high 14.1 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game, leading his team to the bronze medal and being named to the all-tournament team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zach Edey (CAN)'s profile – FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2021 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/player/Zach-Edey |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=July 11, 2021}}</ref>

On May 24, 2022, Edey agreed to a three-year commitment to play with the Canadian senior men's national team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FOURTEEN ATHLETES COMMITTED TO REPRESENT CANADA AS SENIOR MEN'S NATIONAL TEAM SUMMER CORE REVEALED |url=https://www.basketball.ca/news/athletes-committed-to-represent-canada-as-senior-mens-national-team-summer-core-revealed |access-date=May 24, 2022 |website=Canada Basketball}}</ref>

Edey was selected by coach [[Jordi Fernández]] to play in [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], becoming the only college player in the team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/basketball-world-cup-zach-edey-profile-1.6943071|title=Canada's 7-foot-4 secret weapon, Zach Edey, is hiding in plain sight|last=Dichter|first=Myles|publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]]|access-date=August 31, 2023 |date=August 31, 2023}}</ref> On September 3, they qualified to the quarter-finals, securing a berth at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics - Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]], the first Olympics appearance for Team Canada since [[Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2000]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10088193-shai-gilgeous-alexander-on-canada-qualifying-for-olympics-were-a-part-of-history|title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on Canada Qualifying for Olympics: 'We're a Part of History'|last=Rapp|first=Timothy|website=[[The Bleacher Report]]|date=September 3, 2023|access-date=September 10, 2023}}</ref> Canada won the bronze medal over the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] in the third-place game. This was Canada's first-ever World Cup medal, and first medal at a major global tournament since the [[Basketball at the 1936 Summer Olympics|1936 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/article-canada-defeats-us-in-overtime-to-claim-bronze-first-ever-medal-at-fiba/|title=Canada defeats U.S. in overtime to claim bronze, first-ever medal at FIBA World Cup|newspaper=[[The Globe & Mail]]|access-date=September 10, 2023 |date=September 10, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/news/canada-beats-united-states-to-clinch-bronze-at-fiba-world-cup|title=Canada Clinches 1st World Cup Medal With Thrilling Victory Over Americans|last=Rose|first=Aaron|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|access-date=September 10, 2023 |date=September 10, 2023}}</ref>
